indicators.note: accepting means the phrase built from the first two pieces takes the time letter into its middle

parts.note: a criminal is a con, so the criminal's is CON'S
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone trying to grasp a convict's remorse once a sentence has been served.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe a remark is to interpret it, a direct synonym of understand.

clue.text: Old bread prepared, with seed coating

indicators.note: coating means the seed word wraps round the other piece like a husk

parts.note: a pea is a seed
set means prepared, as in all set

explanation.surface: A recipe for a stale loaf finished with a crust of seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, so 'Old bread' is a former currency: the peseta was Spain's money before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and the peseta was Spain's currency until the euro replaced it.

indicators.note: in means the beam word is placed inside the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action
a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: The setter Beam asks whether solvers are pleased to see his puzzle at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Beam is the setter's pseudonym, so the surface reads as a self-reference; here it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Delighted means greatly pleased, a stronger synonym of happy.

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the queen's letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: An angry monarch overthrowing a continental king.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeking is giving off smoke or fumes, which is the literal sense of fuming.

indicators.note: covers means the band word goes round the tango letter

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dance band whose repertoire takes in a set of tangos.
explanation.definitionFit: A stash is a hoarded store of things, a hidden collection.

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word church

parts.note: allowed means authorised or permitted

explanation.surface: A church at last gives approval and declares something holy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed ground is consecrated, made holy, which is what sanctified means.

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly
a lunge is a sudden forward dive or thrust

explanation.surface: Instructions to slip silently into the water and go under.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge something is to thrust or sink it down into liquid, a synonym of submerge.

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone drones on tediously right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the first letters of the four words spell the answer, and the clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore people is to weary them with dull repetition, which is being obnoxiously repetitious.

clue.text: United in tied score at last

indicators.note: in means the United letter is placed inside the tied-score phrase

parts.note: an even tally is a level score
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A football report: United finally manage to draw level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the definition but supplies a single letter; the definition is 'at last' at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means in the end, after some delay, just as at last does.

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is drawn out of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Mark Knopfler of Dire Straits is the star of the Fender Stratocaster guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a guitar hero; the star is the printed symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped mark used in printing.

indicators.note: deserted empties the word sea, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: a line is a channel of communication, as a telephone line

explanation.surface: Salt washed into an abandoned sea passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links definition to wordplay: the answer is found in the pieces that follow. 'sea channel' tempts as one phrase, but 'deserted' works on 'sea' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Saline means salty or containing salt, as in saline solution, so it serves for salt used adjectivally.

indicators.note: round means the swimming word goes around the letters picked from reef

parts.note: bathing is swimming, as in the sea

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of reef, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An uplifting description of swimming around a coral reef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' is meant in its literal sense of drawing air into the lungs, not uplifting.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration in physiology is breathing in, so inspiring literally means drawing breath.

indicators.note: for means one letter is put in place of another in the sentimental word

parts.note: sweet means sentimental, cloyingly so

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word text

explanation.surface: A soppy text message, opening with a gushing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentimental' looks like the definition, but it is SWEET, whose S makes way for T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short post on the social network formerly called Twitter, a kind of message.

clue.text: Sweetheart is proud hugging advanced sweetheart

indicators.note: hugging means the is-proud word wraps around the advanced word

parts.note: to be vain is to be proud of oneself
lent means advanced, as money is
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A lover so conceited that they cling to an equally devoted partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'sweetheart' is read as 'sweet heart', the centre of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is the person chosen as one's love on St Valentine's Day.

clue.text: Resolute with love for one unravelled

indicators.note: with ... for means the love letter takes the place of the one letter

parts.note: decided means resolute or firm
I is the Roman numeral for one
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A determined lover whose relationship nonetheless fell apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoded message has been unravelled, its meaning worked out.

clue.text: One speaks about exercise for worker

indicators.note: about means the speaker word goes around the exercise letters

parts.note: an orator is one who speaks in public
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A speaker lectures on exercise for the benefit of a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator runs a machine or process, so is a kind of worker.

indicators.note: is pronounced signals that the forbidden word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: banned means forbidden
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A sweeping declaration that some kind of dressing is now outlawed, full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material used to dress a wound.

clue.text: Reddish lady after vacation with caution

indicators.note: after places the emptied lady letters behind the reddish word

parts.note: ginger is a reddish hair colour

indicators.note: vacation empties the word lady, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A red-haired woman returning from holiday and being careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptying out lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingerly means carefully and warily, doing something with caution.

clue.text: Lifeless heart cut absorbing current power

indicators.note: absorbing means the shortened heart word takes the two letters into itself
cut lops the final letter off the heart word

parts.note: the inside is the heart of something
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A dead heart, cut open, takes in an electric current to restart it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims INSIDE to INSID, and 'absorbing' puts IP into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid means flat and spiritless, lacking vitality, so lifeless.

clue.text: Strength of donkey with discontented effort

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: discontented empties the word effort, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A donkey's might, combined with a half-hearted, grumbling effort.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a strong point, a strength one can rely on.

parts.note: a haven is a harbour or port

explanation.surface: A little harbour where the ship's crew have been laid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew cut' is the short haircut, not a reduction in a ship's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut, so someone with one is closely shorn.

indicators.note: keeping says the two words hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A princess waiting for something while staying loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means never stopping, continuous, which is a sense of constant.

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds the same as the one the clue describes

parts.note: horseradish is a well-known sauce, served with roast beef

explanation.surface: A query about where horseradish root really comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech SAUCE and SOURCE sound alike; horseradish sauce is a British accompaniment to roast beef.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of a problem is its source, its origin.

clue.text: Greek god is ultimately without end

indicators.note: without end drops the final letter of the phrase

parts.note: at last means ultimately

explanation.surface: A claim that a Greek deity is, in the end, eternal.
explanation.walkthrough: Atlas was strictly a Titan, the one condemned to hold up the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas is the Titan of Greek myth who bore the sky on his shoulders.

indicators.note: to contain means the first container word goes around the second

parts.note: a vat is a large container
a can is a container

explanation.surface: An empty box about to hold another box, like nesting crates.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied or containing nothing, so empty.

clue.text: Burglar is not oddly more startling

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of is not

parts.note: ruder means more abrupt and startling, as in a rude awakening

explanation.surface: A burglar who, strangely, is not the most shocking thing that night.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar breaks into premises uninvited, so is an intruder.

clue.text: Transfer of company rejected in alliance

indicators.note: in places the turned-back company letters inside the alliance word

parts.note: a relation is a connection or alliance, as by marriage

indicators.note: rejected sends the company abbreviation back the other way

explanation.surface: A firm being turned down for a merger and having to move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Relocation is moving someone or something to a new place, a transfer.

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
old means early, as in the old days or Old English

explanation.surface: Catching a chest bug at the very start of winter.
explanation.definitionFit: The common cold is a viral infection of the nose and throat, part of the breathing passages.
